To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
diabetes-induced cardiac contractile dysfunction and intracellular Ca2+ cycling protein abnormalities are ameliorated by cardiac overexpression of metallothionein.

cardiac overexpression of metallothionein alleviated cardiac dysfunction in diabetes, and that this was associated with a decrease in the NADPH oxidases p47(phox), a decrease in the PARP, and a decrease in beta-MHC isoyzymes, but not an increase in SERCA2a.

cardiac overexpression of metallothionein attenuates diabetic cardiomyopathy in mice, possibly through a protective effect against reactive oxygen species and poly(ADPribose) polymerase, and a switch to a fetal myosin heavy-chain isozyme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms by which cardiac dysfunction is induced by diabetes.
the role of metallothionein on cardiac dysfunction in diabetic cardiomyopathy.
understanding the molecular basis of diabetic heart dysfunction and developing new therapeutic strategies to prevent or delay the onset of diabetic heart failure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the beneficial effect of MT is mediated by a mechanism involving NADPH oxidases, PARP activation, and MHC isoform switch.
MT overexpression alleviates cardiac contractile dysfunction in diabetes by attenuating oxidative stress, PARP activation and the MHC isozymic shift.
MT alleviates cardiac dysfunction, in part, by attenuating oxidative stress, PARP activation, and beta-MHC switch in diabetic cardiomyopathy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the overexpression of MT alleviated diabetic cardiomyopathy through a mechanism involving the modulation of NADPH oxidases, PARP and beta-MHC isomyosin switch.

MT alleviates diabetic cardiac dysfunction by modulating the expression of NADPH oxidases and PARP, which are involved in the pathogenesis of diabetes-induced myocardial contractile dysfunction, and by altering the MHC isozymes, which are involved with the pathogenesis of diabetic cardiomyopathies.

MT alleviates diabetic cardiomyopathy by improving cardiac contractile function through the modulation of intracellular Ca( 2+) cycling proteins and the NADPH oxidant system, which in turn attenuate the PARP stress response and beta-MHC isomyosin switch.
The main takeaway from our work is that

metallothionein is a novel therapeutic agent in diabetic cardiomyopathy and the beneficial effect of metallothionein in diabetic heart may be mediated through its anti-oxidative, anti-apoptotic and myosin isozyme switching actions.
metallothionein can protect against diabetic cardiomyopathy by modulating the expression and activity of Ca(2+) transporters, NADPH-oxidase, PARP, and myosin isoforms.
MT may be a useful therapeutic tool in diabetic cardiomyopathy.
